title: Memory of Initial Conditions in Self-Similar Diffusion: A Renormalization-Group Perspective
abstract: Universality is usually associated with asymptotic behavior becoming independent of details of the initial state. Using a unified renormalization-group (RG) framework for self-similar dynamics, we show that retaining relevant length scales leads naturally to distinct classes of memory-retaining fixed points. A modified density-dependent diffusion model reveals a general scaling structure in which initial-condition information remains asymptotically relevant, with the Barenblatt equation emerging as a special case. These results provide a new perspective on universality and anomalous scaling.
summary: This work applies a unified Renormalization Group framework to study self-similar diffusion processes. It demonstrates that whether an initial condition's memory survives the asymptotic limit depends critically on whether the underlying physical model conserves mass. This provides a refined understanding of universality beyond simple scale invariance.
main_problem: The paper investigates how information from initial conditions persists or is lost during self-similar evolution governed by nonlinear diffusion equations.
main_result: For non-conservative systems, the memory of the initial length scale survives the Renormalization Group (RG) flow; conversely, conservative systems exhibit stronger universality where this memory is lost asymptotically.
method: A unified Renormalization Group (RG) framework is employed to analyze scaling dynamics by treating asymptotic solutions as functions of all relevant length scales.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on self-similar diffusion processes, specifically the Density-Dependent Diffusion (DDD) model and its modified version, which are nonlinear partial differential equations.
key_observables: Memory retention of initial length scales ($l$ or $X_0$), scaling exponents ($ eta$, $q$), and the functional dependence on multiple length scales in the asymptotic solution.
important_parameters: Diffusion parameters ($\kappa$), anomalous dimension ($q$), and initial scale factors ($m_0, l$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that self-similar solutions can be characterized by RG Fixed Points (FPs) derived from scale transformations.
paper_structure: The paper develops the unified RG framework for scaling dynamics, applies it to the DDD model showing memory loss in the conservative case, and then analyzes the modified DDD model where non-conservation forces the retention of initial condition memory.
why_interesting: While focused on classical PDEs, the concept of scale invariance breaking down due to retained initial conditions mirrors complex phenomena in open quantum systems or strongly correlated materials where boundary effects or finite size are crucial.
